title: Cà Phê Trứng
subtitle: vietnamese egg coffee
excerpt: Cà phê trứng is a Hanoi speciality of strong Vietnamese coffee topped with a thick, creamy foam made from egg yolks and condensed milk. The result is like a tiramisu in a cup. This recipe serves 2.
sourceNotes: Cà phê trứng was invented at Giảng Café in Hanoi in the 1940s when fresh milk was scarce and egg was used as a substitute. The café still serves the original recipe today.

glossaryTerms.definition: Vietnamese coffee is typically made from robusta beans, which are stronger and more bitter than arabica. It is brewed using a small metal drip filter called a phin and served over condensed milk.
A small Vietnamese metal coffee drip filter that sits on top of a glass. Hot water is poured over the grounds and drips slowly into the cup below, making a very concentrated brew.

content.text: Cà phê trứng is strong
cà phê
topped with a thick, sweet egg foam.
The egg yolk is whisked with condensed milk until it forms a pale, creamy mousse that floats on the hot coffee.
This recipe serves 2.
If you do not have a
phin
filter, use a very strong espresso or 4 tablespoons of strong cafetière coffee per person.
What you need

items.prepNote: strong dark roast, ground for drip or espresso

content.text: Method
Brew the coffee using your preferred method. Make it as strong as possible . about 80 ml per person. Keep it very hot.

Place the egg yolks and condensed milk in a heatproof bowl. Set over a small saucepan of barely simmering water. Whisk vigorously for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is very pale, thick, and doubled in volume.
Remove from the heat. The foam should hold its shape when the whisk is lifted.
Divide the hot coffee between 2 small cups or glasses.
Spoon the egg foam generously over the top of each coffee. The foam should float on the surface.
Serve immediately. Do not stir . drink through the foam, which melts slowly into the coffee as you drink.

attrs.symptom: The egg foam is thin and liquid instead of thick and mousse-like.
attrs.cause: The yolks were not whisked enough or were too cold.
attrs.fix: Use room-temperature eggs and whisk over the hot water bath for the full 3 to 4 minutes. The mixture must reach a ribbon-like consistency.

attrs.symptom: The foam tastes eggy and raw.
attrs.cause: The eggs were not cooked enough over the heat.
attrs.fix: Keep the water bath at a gentle simmer and whisk for the full time. The heat partially cooks the yolks, which removes the raw taste.

attrs.symptom: The foam sinks into the coffee immediately.
attrs.cause: The foam was not thick enough or the coffee was too hot.
attrs.fix: Whisk longer to build a thicker foam. Let the coffee cool for 1 minute before topping - if the coffee is boiling, it melts the foam too fast.

content.text: Where this dish lives
Cà phê trứng was created in Hanoi in the 1940s and is most closely associated with that city.
Giảng Café in the Old Quarter is credited with inventing the drink.
It was created as a way to make a creamy coffee drink when fresh dairy was scarce during wartime.
Today it is served at cafés throughout Hanoi and has become famous internationally.
Visitors to Hanoi list it as one of the most memorable drinks they try.
